svg.title: IDoc production architecture
svg.desc: Five trust zones, ordered by what an attacker holding the previous one can reach: the public internet, the nginx edge, the application, isolated execution for student code, and the restricted database that holds every education record.
svg.text: verified against the running deployment · 2026-08-20 · commit ef15e5e2 / main
generated by scripts/build-architecture.mjs — do not hand-edit
session cookie only — no client cert
folder or Drive workspace held here
no CDN, no proxy in front
no inbound path into the stack
absent → Drive falls back to server
api keyed on $cookie_idoc_sid, not the IP —
a lecture theatre is ONE NAT address
a hashed name IS the cache key
what a hostile page needs omitted
npm run security checks every one
loopback — the app is not on a public interface
a PDF no longer freezes the event loop
the host holds only the PUBLIC half —
it cannot read its own history
NO off-host copy yet — losing the VM
the anchor prints to STDOUT, so systemd
captures it — a logger call inside the
today 10.162.0.6:4300 on the forge; falls back to the local runner over idoc_backend, which has no route out
no published port; only app reaches
an auth bug in the app cannot become
code execution next to the database
so a lecture pressing Run does not
scram-sha-256 — the ONLY path to the records
not a copy of anything else
metadata answers 200, so the ops agent
still reports — that gap is known
Elsewhere in ru-knowsy — deliberately not on the path above
NO nginx, on purpose: the app binds
127.0.0.1:4173 and the only way in is
CONTAINER on its own compose network,
is why this row used to read as though
education records. It holds 1 test user,
NO DNS NAME POINTS AT IT YET
listed only so that nobody later
mistakes it for an orphan and
